culture: Piazza Navona is a famous square in Rome where artists paint daily
Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers stands in Piazza Navona
Legend says one river god covers his eyes in fear of the church (Sant'Agnese), though it is only a story
Many street painters work in the square, each with their own style, using oil paints and easels
The square's long oval shape comes from the ancient Stadium of Domitian that once stood there
Fewer crowds visit in November
Street paintings are hand-painted and sold directly in the square, e.g. for around thirty euros
Italian idiom 'buttare i soldi dalla finestra' means to waste money (throw money out the window)
The Befana Christmas market is held in Piazza Navona in December and the square is full of lights
Formal address in Italian uses 'Lei' (e.g. 'Le piace?', 'Vuole vedere?')
Common greetings and phrases: Buongiorno, Grazie mille, A presto, Buona giornata

Chestnut (castagne) flavours are a winter seasonal treat, around December
Italian shopkeepers use formal address (Lei) with customers, e.g. 'Le piace?'
Common polite phrases: Buongiorno, grazie, a presto, ottima scelta, prego/provi pure
